title: Swirling stars above the VLT
caption: Swirling star trails above the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars appear to swirl in circles above the enclosures of ESO's Very Large Telescope at Paranal in this photograph of the rotating night sky.

The stars are not really moving in loops. The effect comes from the way the picture was made: the photographer used a very long exposure, keeping the camera's shutter open while the Earth turned beneath the sky. As our planet rotates, the stars seem to glide slowly across the heavens, and over a long exposure each one leaves a curved streak of light in the image.

The result turns a still scene into a record of time passing. The telescope enclosures stay fixed and sharp in the foreground, because they turn along with the Earth, while the sky behind them wheels around. It is a reminder that every observation made from the ground is taken from a spinning platform, and that telescopes must steadily track the stars to keep them in view.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph at ESO's Paranal Observatory, in visible light, using a very long exposure. The exact camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points at any moment; only a very long exposure turns the Earth's rotation into swirling trails.
